title: VPC asymmetric routing caused control plane API failures during private upgrade - postmortem & action items
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: During a private VPC control plane upgrade, a subset of customer VPCs experienced control plane API timeouts caused by asymmetric routing introduced by a partial BGP policy change on the upgrade path. The incident led to ~30 min of degraded API availability for affected customers and several escalations. This ticket captures the timeline, root cause analysis, short-term mitigations, and prioritized action items for full remediation.
timeline: 2026-03-11 01:12 UTC - Upgrade job started for private control plane nodes in us-west-2 region.
2026-03-11 01:34 UTC - First control plane 504s observed from customer monitoring; paging triggered for SRE/Platform on-call.
2026-03-11 01:40 UTC - Engineers confirmed API timeouts correlated with control plane nodes updated to 2026.03.0 build.

2026-03-11 01:55 UTC - Scoped to VPCs using BGP-based routing with egress via peering appliances; traffic captures showed SYN packets reaching control plane but responses routed over a different AS path.
2026-03-11 02:10 UTC - Rolled back the partial BGP route advertisement change on the upgrade path; control plane API latency returned to normal over next ~10 minutes.
2026-03-11 02:25 UTC - Confirmed rollback restored symmetric routing for affected VPCs; incident declared resolved but follow-ups assigned for full RCA and fixes.
2026-03-11 03:00 UTC - Incident report posted to #incidents and customer-facing incident summary drafted for outreach team.
root_cause: A partial BGP policy change deployed as part of the upgrade sequence caused an asymmetric routing condition for traffic between certain private VPCs and control plane nodes. The change altered route selection for return paths (different AS path via an intermediate transit appliance) so replies to control plane API requests did not return on the same path, triggering connection tracking / firewall state mismatches and resulting in API timeouts. The underlying code/upgrade was valid for most topologies, but our preflight checks did not detect this combination of customer BGP topologies and the partial deployment order introduced the transient asymmetry.
mitigations: Immediate rollback of the BGP advertisement change on the upgrade path (completed 2026-03-11 02:10 UTC).
Temporary stop of further upgrades for regions where BGP peering transit appliances are present until route-policy verification is added to the upgrade job.
Notified affected customers with summary and guidance; support follow-ups scheduled to verify network state on customer side.
long_term_actions: (P0) Implement a pre-upgrade topology verifier that simulates route propagation and flags potential asymmetric-return-paths for VPCs using BGP peering - owner: Jonah Kim - due: 2026-03-25.
(P0) Add canary sequencing to the upgrade pipeline that ensures route-policy changes are applied and validated on a small transit set before broader rollout - owner: SRE Squad - due: 2026-04-05.

(P1) Enhance control plane health checks to include TCP connection validation from multiple AS paths and fail upgrade if asymmetric connectivity is detected - owner: Runtime Networking - due: 2026-04-12.
(P1) Create a runbook for asymmetric routing incidents detailing packet-capture triage steps, rollback checklist, and customer communication templates - owner: Platform Reliability - due: 2026-03-20.
(P2) Coordinate with Solutions Engineering to update private deployment onboarding docs to capture common BGP topologies and recommended route policies - owner: SE Team - due: 2026-05-01.
owners: Jonah Kim - lead investigator / networking fixes
Marta Rivera - SRE coordination and rollback lead
Priya Sharma - customer communications and post-incident outreach
notes: Decision: We chose rollback over progressive traffic engineering because customers were experiencing meaningful timeouts and rollback restored capacity within minutes.
Trade-off: Introducing additional preflight checks will add ~2-4 minutes to the upgrade window; acceptable to avoid customer impact for private deployments.
Follow-up: Explore a lightweight BGP simulation that can run fast as part of preflight rather than a full BGP convergence test.
